title: Searching and Evaluating Publications and Preprints Using Europe PMC
author: Rosonovski, Levchenko, et al.

steps.title: Open Europe PMC homepage
steps.instruction: Open the Europe PMC website at http://europepmc.org in a web browser of your choice.

steps.title: Perform basic keyword search
steps.instruction: In the main search bar type a keyword or a string of terms (e.g., “metastatic bone cancer”) and click the Search button. The search is case‑insensitive, removes stop words (e.g., “a”, “on”, “is”) and most punctuation, and returns all records (journal articles and preprints) where the terms appear in abstracts, metadata, or full text; references are excluded.

steps.title: Use exact‑phrase search (optional)
steps.instruction: Enclose the exact phrase in quotation marks (e.g., “tRNA function”) to retrieve only records where the words appear in that exact order. Stop words are retained for exact‑phrase searches.

steps.title: Review search results page
steps.instruction: The results page shows the total number of hits, the first 25 results, navigation to further pages, and options to change sort order, export results, or apply filters. For each record the title, authors, journal or preprint server, volume, issue, pagination, publication date, and identifiers (PMID, PMCID, PPR) are displayed when available.

steps.title: Review search snippets for relevance
steps.instruction: Examine the bolded keywords in the snippet under each result to gauge context. Click a title to open the article, scroll down to “Occurrences of search terms within full text” to see excerpts, and click a snippet to jump to that location in the full text.

steps.title: Refine results – sort order
steps.instruction: Use the “Sort by” drop‑down menu to select Relevance (default), Most recently added, Times cited, or Date published. Relevance ranking favours high term frequency, many distinct terms, rare terms, short articles, and recent publication dates.

steps.title: Refine results – filters
steps.instruction:
Apply filters as needed:
- Type: choose Research article, Review, or Preprint (Preprints can be further limited with the “Journal published” sub‑filter).
- Free full text: select “Free to read” (free full text in Europe PMC) or “Free to read and use” (Creative Commons‑like license).
- Date: pick one or more recent years, or use “Custom date range” to enter start and end years and click the search icon.
- Boolean operators: combine terms with AND, OR, NOT (e.g., microvesicles AND exercise).

steps.title: Access an article
steps.instruction: Click the title hyperlink on the results page to open the article page. Use the left navigation bar to select “Free full text” (if available) or “Full text”. Icons indicate source: green padlock for a free external copy, external‑link icon for the publisher site. As of September 2022, over 8.1 million records have free full text in Europe PMC, supplemented by Unpaywall.

steps.title: Download PDF of free full text
steps.instruction: When free full text is present, click the “Open PDF” option in the Tools bar on the right‑hand side.

steps.title: Browse article sections and figures
steps.instruction: Use the left navigation bar (after expanding the Free full text area) to jump to sections such as Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. To view figures, select the “Figures” section or scroll below the abstract; click thumbnails to expand, view legends, or use “Show in full text”. Figure carousel appears only when the article license permits reuse.

steps.title: Use Annotations panel
steps.instruction: Open the “Annotations” panel from the right‑hand Tools bar. Select one or more annotation types (e.g., diseases, chemicals, genes) to highlight occurrences in the text. Use the “Find” option to jump to the next mention. Highlighting works only on abstracts/full‑text with a reusable license.

steps.title: Evaluate article status
steps.instruction: Identify preprints by the green “Preprint” label and orange notification box. Click the “journal published article” link in the notification to view the peer‑reviewed version (if available). Access version history via the “Preprint version history” dropdown; the current version is shown with the green label. Note that some servers (e.g., bioRxiv, medRxiv) may not provide version history.

steps.title: View reviews and impact metrics
steps.instruction: Select “Reviews” in the left navigation bar to see open peer‑review materials from services such as Publons, Faculty Opinions, preLights, Peer Community In, PREreview, Sciety. Choose “Citations & impact” to see yearly citation counts, Altmetric donut, scite.ai smart citations, and a list of citing articles (displayed only if at least one citation exists in Europe PMC).

steps.title: Search by author
steps.instruction: Enter an author’s last name and first name or initials (e.g., “John Smith” or “Smith J”) in the main search bar. Up to two matching authors appear in the “Suggested authors” box (requires a public ORCID and at least one Europe PMC record). Click a suggested name to search by ORCID, or type the ORCID identifier directly (e.g., 0000‑0002‑1611‑6935) to restrict results to that author’s public publications.

steps.title: Find a specific article by title or advanced search
steps.instruction: Paste the exact article title into the main search bar (e.g., “Protecting the Mitochondria in Cardiac Disease”) and keep sort order set to Relevance. For more complex queries, click the “Advanced search” link below the main bar. In the Bibliographic Fields section, fill in Title (exact phrase), Journal, Author, Publication year, etc.; add additional authors with the “+” button. Click the top‑page Search button.

steps.title: Search methodology in specific sections
steps.instruction: From the Advanced search page, scroll to the “Filters” section, expand “Article Sections”, choose a section type (e.g., Materials & Methods, Supplementary Data, Figures, Tables) from the drop‑down, enter keywords or phrases, and add more sections with the “+” button if desired. Click the bottom “Search” button. Results are limited to full‑text articles/preprints; multiple sections are combined with Boolean AND unless OR/NOT is selected.

steps.title: Perform advanced annotation search
steps.instruction: On the Advanced search page, scroll to the “Annotations” section, select an Annotation Type (e.g., Gene–Disease associations, Protein‑protein interactions, Phosphorylation) from the drop‑down, add more types with the “+” button, and click Search. To explore a highlighted annotation in an article, hover over it to open a pop‑up with a link to the source database (e.g., IntAct for protein interactions).

steps.title: Locate data behind a publication
steps.instruction: On the article page, use the left navigation bar to open the “Data” section. The “Data behind the article” subsection lists supplemental material links, data accession numbers, and DOIs; click any hyperlink to open the external repository (e.g., PDBe entry 2p1l). The “Data that cites the article” subsection shows external databases (e.g., FlyBase, UniProt, ChEMBL) that reference the article.

steps.title: Find data citations or database‑cited articles
steps.instruction: In Advanced search, scroll to “Data Links and Data Citations”. Under “Find data citations in the abstract or full text of articles”, select a citation type (e.g., functional genomics), add more with “+”, and click Search. Under “Find articles cited in a database”, choose a database (e.g., FlyBase, UniProt, OMIM), add more with “+”, and click Search.

steps.title: Expand reading list and build bibliography
steps.instruction:
• Access cited references: expand “Free full text” → “References”; click “[Europe PMC free article]”, “[Abstract]”, “[Crossref]”, or “[Google Scholar]” links.
• View citing articles: go to “Citations & impact” → “Article citations” → click “Go to all [n] article citations”.
• View similar articles: select “Similar articles” in the left navigation.
• Export citations: on an article page, click “Get citation” in the right toolbar and choose format (BibTex, RIS, .txt, XML, NLM). On the search results page, click “Export citations” on the left, select up to 50,000 records, choose a format, and download.

steps.title: Create email alert for new literature
steps.instruction: On the results page, click “Save & create alert” beside the main search bar. Sign in with an ORCID, Twitter, or Europe PMC account (required to provide an email address). In the alert form, edit the alert name if desired, choose delivery frequency (as soon as available, weekly, or monthly), set a preferred day for weekly/monthly alerts, and select email content (title‑author‑journal only or include a partial abstract). Alerts are sent at approximately 06:00 GMT.
